references.text: Direct quote from [ref:Sal 118:22-23|Psalm 118:22-23]. Jesus quotes this psalm verse about the stone that the builders rejected, which has become the cornerstone, and applies it to himself as the rejected Messiah.
[ref:Jes 28:16|Isaiah 28:16] prophesies about a precious cornerstone that God lays in Zion. This prophecy completes the picture of the stone that Jesus uses in the parable.
Parallel passage in [ref:Matt 21:42|Matthew 21:42] where Jesus quotes the same verse from Psalm 118 in connection with the parable of the vineyard and the wicked tenants.
Parallel passage in [ref:Mark 12:10-11|Mark 12:10-11] where Jesus similarly concludes the parable of the vineyard with the quote from Psalm 118 about the rejected cornerstone.
In [ref:Apg 4:11|Acts 4:11], Peter applies this same scripture directly to Jesus Christ, saying that he is the stone which was rejected by the builders but has become the cornerstone.

[ref:1 Pet 2:4-7|1 Peter 2:4-7] gathers several stone texts from the Old Testament, including Psalm 118:22, and applies them to Christ as the living stone—rejected by people but chosen and precious to God.
[ref:Ef 2:20|Ephesians 2:20] describes Christ Jesus as the cornerstone in the building that is founded on the foundation of the apostles and prophets—a continuation of the cornerstone motif.
[ref:Rom 9:33|Romans 9:33] combines Isaiah texts about the stone in Zion and applies it to Christ as a stumbling stone for those who do not believe, but a foundation for those who believe.
